scope: All 191 catalogue/model IDs checked for uniqueness, finite anchors, playable bounds, source/render tile ownership and missing dimension metadata. This is not 191 photo-verified reconstructions.

symbolAudit.notes: One national-flag recipe found; uses shared official-specification geometry.

Four articulated back-to-back lions and four outward24-spoke wheels replace gold boxes; primary government description supports the basic form. Exact reliefs, motto and site sculpture details remain open.
Temple owner explicitly specifies eight spokes; dated original photos confirm open-wheel finials. Fine ornament remains approximate.

Gurdwara cloth now hangs folded near its mast and has a spearhead finial supported by Sikh Rehat Maryada. A hidden printed Khanda is not inferred. Current site colour and flag dimensions remain open. Jagannath pennants retain original-photo colours without invented symbols.
Official unveiling photo supports green sari/red blouse, raised right palm and left crop bundle. Exact likeness and inherited scale/anchor remain provisional.
Dated frontal photo confirms right palm raised, left hand at collar and stone lotus; exact sculpture/reliefs remain stylised.
Generic human silhouettes do not establish portrait accuracy. No speculative sacred text or inscriptions introduced.
